name: Rider–Waite–Smith
credit: Pamela Colman Smith, working with Arthur Edward Waite. Pam-A printing, circa 1910. Scans from the TaionWC collection on Wikimedia Commons.
rights: The Wikimedia Commons record for each bundled scan carries the Public Domain Mark. Card commentaries are original to this app.

cards.title: The Fool
cards.symbolism: A traveler's foot meets the edge of a cliff while a small dog springs beside him.
cards.meaning: Begin with curiosity. Give the first step your attention before committing to the whole journey.
cards.reversed: Excitement can hide a drop. Check your footing or name the fear that keeps you at the starting point.

cards.title: The Magician
cards.symbolism: One hand lifts a wand while the other points down toward the tools on the table.
cards.meaning: Bring an idea into practice using one skill or resource already within reach.
cards.reversed: Notice where persuasive words have taken the place of action. Try a small demonstration.

cards.title: The High Priestess
cards.symbolism: Between two pillars, a seated figure partly conceals a scroll behind her mantle.
cards.meaning: Leave room for an impression to develop before you explain it. Listen to what keeps returning.
cards.reversed: A hunch may be tangled with an assumption. Find a quiet way to test the difference.

cards.title: The Empress
cards.symbolism: A crowned figure rests beside a field of grain. The wheat gives abundance a material form.
cards.meaning: Care for the conditions that let something grow. Nourishment takes time and attention.
cards.reversed: Notice whether giving has exhausted the giver. Restore one source of comfort or support.

cards.title: The Emperor
cards.symbolism: A stone throne carved with rams anchors the ruler against bare mountains.
cards.meaning: Give a fragile plan enough structure to survive a difficult day.
cards.reversed: A rule can outlive its purpose. Change the boundary that no longer protects anyone.

cards.title: The Hierophant
cards.symbolism: Two figures receive instruction beneath crossed keys at the teacher's feet.
cards.meaning: Seek out a tradition or teacher and learn the reasoning behind a practice.
cards.reversed: A borrowed rule may fit poorly. Decide which parts still deserve your trust.

cards.title: The Lovers
cards.symbolism: Two people stand beneath a winged figure, with a mountain between their trees.
cards.meaning: Let shared values guide a choice. Say aloud what each person hopes to protect.
cards.reversed: Conflicting values need an honest conversation before another promise.

cards.title: The Chariot
cards.symbolism: A light sphinx and a dark sphinx face forward beneath the charioteer's canopy.
cards.meaning: Coordinate competing impulses around a clear destination.
cards.reversed: Forcing progress in two directions drains energy. Choose the next turn deliberately.

cards.title: Strength
cards.symbolism: A figure in a white dress gently holds a lion's jaws beneath a loop of infinity.
cards.meaning: Use steadiness and patience to meet strong feelings. Gentleness can hold a boundary.
cards.reversed: Look for strain disguised as composure. Take a pause before trying to master the feeling.

cards.title: The Hermit
cards.symbolism: An old traveler holds a star inside a lantern at the top of a snowy height.
cards.meaning: Step back far enough to hear your own judgment. Identify one thing your experience can illuminate.
cards.reversed: Time alone may have become a habit. Bring one insight back into conversation.

cards.title: Wheel of Fortune
cards.symbolism: A turning wheel carries rising and falling figures between four winged readers.
cards.meaning: A change in timing can open possibilities. Distinguish what turns by chance from what you can choose.
cards.reversed: Notice a repeating pattern and act on the part of it you can interrupt.

cards.title: Justice
cards.symbolism: An upright sword and level scales place decision and deliberation in the same pair of hands.
cards.meaning: Balance the evidence, name your responsibility and make a decision you can explain.
cards.reversed: An uneven standard may be shaping the outcome. Consider whose evidence went unheard.

cards.title: The Hanged Man
cards.symbolism: A man hangs by one foot, his face calm within a bright halo.
cards.meaning: An intentional pause can reveal an angle hidden by urgency. Revisit the question from another position.
cards.reversed: Waiting without a purpose can harden into delay. Name what could make the pause worthwhile.

cards.title: Death
cards.symbolism: A skeleton rides beneath a white rose banner as the sun appears between two towers.
cards.meaning: Allow an ending to be real. Make space for what the old arrangement could no longer support.
cards.reversed: Something may be lingering after its purpose has ended. Choose a small act of closure.

cards.title: Temperance
cards.symbolism: With one foot on land and one in water, an angel pours from cup to cup.
cards.meaning: Find a workable proportion between two needs by experimenting a little at a time.
cards.reversed: One ingredient may be overwhelming the blend. Change the pace or amount.

cards.title: The Devil
cards.symbolism: Two figures wear loose chains below a horned figure on a dark pedestal.
cards.meaning: Examine the bargain behind a habit. Locate one link that you have the power to loosen.
cards.reversed: Recognizing a familiar pattern creates a chance to try another response.

cards.title: The Tower
cards.symbolism: Lightning strikes a crowned tower, scattering sparks and two falling figures.
cards.meaning: An unexpected change exposes a weak assumption. Start with what remains sound.
cards.reversed: A disruption may be unfolding quietly. Attend to the first visible crack.

cards.title: The Star
cards.symbolism: Below a large star, a kneeling figure pours water onto the earth and into a pool.
cards.meaning: Choose a modest, repeatable act that restores hope after strain.
cards.reversed: When encouragement feels distant, give yourself a concrete sign of progress to notice.

cards.title: The Moon
cards.symbolism: A path runs between two towers while a crustacean rises from water toward two animals.
cards.meaning: Move carefully through uncertainty. Record what you perceive before deciding what it means.
cards.reversed: Separate a fading fear from new information as the scene grows clearer.

cards.title: The Sun
cards.symbolism: A child on a white horse carries a red banner past tall sunflowers.
cards.meaning: Share a visible success. Let openness and simple enjoyment have their place.
cards.reversed: A muted celebration still counts. Adjust expectations enough to recognize the good at hand.

cards.title: Judgement
cards.symbolism: People rise with lifted arms to the sound of an angel's trumpet.
cards.meaning: Answer a call to reassess an old story. Choose what you will do differently with the insight.
cards.reversed: A harsh inner verdict can drown out the invitation to change. Start with a fairer account.

cards.title: The World
cards.symbolism: A dancing figure holds two wands inside a leafy wreath framed by four creatures.
cards.meaning: Recognize a cycle that has reached its shape. Gather what you learned before beginning again.
cards.reversed: An unfinished detail may be keeping a chapter open. Identify what would count as completion.

cards.title: Ace of Wands
cards.symbolism: A cloud-borne hand holds a leafy staff above a broad landscape.
cards.meaning: Try the first concrete action suggested by a spark of enthusiasm.
cards.reversed: A promising impulse may need rest, timing or a more specific outlet.

cards.title: Two of Wands
cards.symbolism: Between two staffs, a figure looks over the water with a globe in hand.
cards.meaning: Consider the scale of a plan and what it would take to leave familiar ground.
cards.reversed: Bring a distant ambition down to a decision you can make here.

cards.title: Three of Wands
cards.symbolism: Three planted staffs surround a figure watching ships at sea.
cards.meaning: Look beyond the initial effort and prepare to meet its results.
cards.reversed: Recheck timing and resources when the expected return is slow.

cards.title: Four of Wands
cards.symbolism: A flowering garland hangs across four staffs as people gather beyond.
cards.meaning: Mark a milestone with the people who helped create a place of welcome.
cards.reversed: A celebration may need a different form to include the people who matter.

cards.title: Five of Wands
cards.symbolism: Five young figures cross staffs in a crowded field of movement.
cards.meaning: Use disagreement to discover where aims and methods diverge.
cards.reversed: Lower the noise enough to identify the actual dispute.

cards.title: Six of Wands
cards.symbolism: A rider carries a laurel-crowned staff before a group of companions.
cards.meaning: Accept recognition and acknowledge the people behind a victory.
cards.reversed: Define success independently of applause that may be slow to arrive.

cards.title: Seven of Wands
cards.symbolism: One person on high ground holds off six staffs rising from below.
cards.meaning: Defend a position that matters and choose where your effort will count.
cards.reversed: Too many simultaneous challenges can exhaust a worthy defense. Seek support.

cards.title: Eight of Wands
cards.symbolism: Eight staffs fly diagonally across open sky toward a river landscape.
cards.meaning: Events are gathering speed. Send the message or take the next coordinated step.
cards.reversed: A delay may expose a missed detail. Confirm direction before accelerating.

cards.title: Nine of Wands
cards.symbolism: A bandaged figure watches from behind a line of staffs.
cards.meaning: Draw on experience while conserving enough strength for the final stretch.
cards.reversed: Check whether vigilance has continued beyond the danger.

cards.title: Ten of Wands
cards.symbolism: A bent figure carries a bundle of ten staffs toward a settlement.
cards.meaning: Assess the load you have agreed to carry and arrange the last part of the journey.
cards.reversed: Return a responsibility that belongs elsewhere or divide it into smaller loads.

cards.title: Page of Wands
cards.symbolism: A young traveler studies a budding staff in a dry landscape.
cards.meaning: Experiment while the idea is fresh. Curiosity can supply the first lesson.
cards.reversed: Narrow scattered enthusiasm to one small experiment.

cards.title: Knight of Wands
cards.symbolism: A rider in a salamander-patterned coat raises his staff on a rearing horse.
cards.meaning: Channel restlessness into decisive movement toward a clear objective.
cards.reversed: Slow the charge long enough to see who or what it could overtake.

cards.title: Queen of Wands
cards.symbolism: The queen holds a sunflower and a sprouting staff above a black cat.
cards.meaning: Let warmth and confidence encourage another person's participation.
cards.reversed: Protect your creative energy when being available to everyone becomes tiring.

cards.title: King of Wands
cards.symbolism: The king turns on a throne decorated with lions and salamanders.
cards.meaning: Set a direction and give others the confidence to act within it.
cards.reversed: Make space for other people's methods when your vision becomes too commanding.

cards.title: Ace of Cups
cards.symbolism: A hand offers an overflowing cup above a pool of water lilies.
cards.meaning: Welcome the first stirrings of feeling, affection or creative interest.
cards.reversed: Strong feelings may need a private outlet before they can be shared.

cards.title: Two of Cups
cards.symbolism: Two people lift cups between them below a winged lion and entwined serpents.
cards.meaning: Meet someone halfway. A small reciprocal gesture can deepen trust.
cards.reversed: Check whether both parties understand the exchange in the same way.

cards.title: Three of Cups
cards.symbolism: Three companions raise cups over a harvest of fruit.
cards.meaning: Celebrate with people who have helped something grow.
cards.reversed: Consider whether a group dynamic is leaving someone on the edge.

cards.title: Four of Cups
cards.symbolism: A seated person looks down as a hand offers a fourth cup from a cloud.
cards.meaning: Take time to recognize what you genuinely want before accepting another offer.
cards.reversed: An unnoticed possibility may deserve a second look.

cards.title: Five of Cups
cards.symbolism: A cloaked figure faces three spilled cups while two stand behind.
cards.meaning: Give disappointment its due and notice what is still available.
cards.reversed: Let a remaining relationship or resource become part of the recovery.

cards.title: Six of Cups
cards.symbolism: A taller figure offers a flower-filled cup to a smaller companion.
cards.meaning: Revisit a memory or simple kindness that can nourish the present.
cards.reversed: Question whether a fond memory is setting an impossible standard for today.

cards.title: Seven of Cups
cards.symbolism: Seven cups float among clouds, each holding a different vision.
cards.meaning: Explore the alternatives and compare what each would require in practice.
cards.reversed: Reduce a dazzling list to one choice you can actually try.

cards.title: Eight of Cups
cards.symbolism: A traveler leaves stacked cups behind and walks toward the hills.
cards.meaning: A familiar investment may have given all it can. Follow the need that remains unmet.
cards.reversed: Pause at the threshold and distinguish reluctance to leave from a genuine reason to stay.

cards.title: Nine of Cups
cards.symbolism: A seated figure folds his arms before a curved display of nine cups.
cards.meaning: Acknowledge a wish fulfilled and the work that made it possible.
cards.reversed: Ask whether the reward satisfies the wish that motivated it.

cards.title: Ten of Cups
cards.symbolism: A family stands below a rainbow of cups beside a distant home.
cards.meaning: Notice the everyday gestures that sustain a sense of belonging.
cards.reversed: Let people describe happiness for themselves when a shared ideal feels strained.

cards.title: Page of Cups
cards.symbolism: A fish peers out of the young figure's cup as if starting a conversation.
cards.meaning: Respond playfully to an unexpected feeling or invitation.
cards.reversed: Give a tender idea a little privacy while it develops.

cards.title: Knight of Cups
cards.symbolism: A mounted rider holds a cup steady as he approaches a stream.
cards.meaning: Give an imaginative or heartfelt offer a form another person can receive.
cards.reversed: A graceful promise needs a practical next step.

cards.title: Queen of Cups
cards.symbolism: A queen studies an ornate covered cup at the edge of the sea.
cards.meaning: Give careful attention to a feeling without rushing to interpret it for someone else.
cards.reversed: A boundary can protect your capacity to listen.

cards.title: King of Cups
cards.symbolism: The king holds his cup on a throne surrounded by restless water.
cards.meaning: Steady yourself enough to respond with compassion under pressure.
cards.reversed: Unspoken emotion may be steering a decision. Give it a name.

cards.title: Ace of Swords
cards.symbolism: A hand raises a crowned sword above distant mountain peaks.
cards.meaning: State the question precisely and follow the clearest evidence.
cards.reversed: A sharp argument may need better facts or gentler delivery.

cards.title: Two of Swords
cards.symbolism: A blindfolded figure crosses two swords beside dark water.
cards.meaning: Identify the choice you are holding in balance and seek the missing information.
cards.reversed: Name the cost of postponing the decision once more.

cards.title: Three of Swords
cards.symbolism: Three swords pierce a heart against a rainy sky.
cards.meaning: Acknowledge a painful truth directly enough to begin caring for the wound.
cards.reversed: Give grief time to move without forcing a tidy conclusion.

cards.title: Four of Swords
cards.symbolism: A recumbent figure lies below three swords, with a fourth along the tomb.
cards.meaning: Withdraw from the immediate contest and let rest restore perspective.
cards.reversed: An uneasy pause may call for more support or a gradual return to activity.

cards.title: Five of Swords
cards.symbolism: One figure gathers swords while two others turn toward the water.
cards.meaning: Ask what a victory costs the relationship around it.
cards.reversed: Put down an unnecessary contest and see whether repair is possible.

cards.title: Six of Swords
cards.symbolism: A boatman ferries two passengers and six swords across the water.
cards.meaning: Accept a passage away from difficulty, carrying what experience has taught you.
cards.reversed: An unresolved issue may have traveled with you. Name it before the next crossing.

cards.title: Seven of Swords
cards.symbolism: A figure carries five swords away from an encampment and glances back.
cards.meaning: Plan carefully and examine how secrecy affects the people involved.
cards.reversed: A concealed detail may need to be brought into an honest conversation.

cards.title: Eight of Swords
cards.symbolism: A blindfolded, bound figure stands within a loose enclosure of swords.
cards.meaning: Identify one real constraint and one assumption you can question.
cards.reversed: A small opening can restore a sense of choice. Test it with support.

cards.title: Nine of Swords
cards.symbolism: A figure sits upright in bed beneath nine swords.
cards.meaning: Bring a recurring worry into words so it can be shared and examined.
cards.reversed: Notice a worry losing its grip and strengthen whatever helped.

cards.title: Ten of Swords
cards.symbolism: Ten swords cross a prone figure beneath a dark sky with a bright horizon.
cards.meaning: Recognize an exhausted course of action and conserve strength for what follows.
cards.reversed: Recovery may begin by releasing the need to replay the ending.

cards.title: Page of Swords
cards.symbolism: A watchful youth holds a sword upright in a gusty landscape.
cards.meaning: Ask a precise question and verify what you hear.
cards.reversed: Pause before passing on a claim you have only partly checked.

cards.title: Knight of Swords
cards.symbolism: A knight drives forward with sword raised while trees bend in the wind.
cards.meaning: Commit energy to a clear argument or an urgent task.
cards.reversed: Haste may have outrun understanding. Check the premise before pressing on.

cards.title: Queen of Swords
cards.symbolism: The queen extends one hand while holding a sword upright in the other.
cards.meaning: Pair a clear boundary with an invitation to speak honestly.
cards.reversed: Review whether a necessary distinction has hardened into an unfair judgment.

cards.title: King of Swords
cards.symbolism: The king faces forward with an upright sword and a steady gaze.
cards.meaning: Apply a principle consistently and explain your reasoning.
cards.reversed: Invite scrutiny where authority or certainty has gone unchallenged.

cards.title: Ace of Pentacles
cards.symbolism: A hand presents a gold pentacle above a garden path and gateway.
cards.meaning: Give a practical opportunity the time and resources needed to take root.
cards.reversed: Check the terms of an offer before investing effort or money.

cards.title: Two of Pentacles
cards.symbolism: A figure juggles two coins joined by a figure-eight ribbon before rolling seas.
cards.meaning: Find a workable rhythm between two demands and keep room to adjust.
cards.reversed: Simplify the schedule when constant switching starts costing more than it saves.

cards.title: Three of Pentacles
cards.symbolism: A craftsperson works beneath an arch while two people consult beside it.
cards.meaning: Combine complementary skills and agree on what good workmanship looks like.
cards.reversed: Clarify roles or standards when collaborators keep missing one another.

cards.title: Four of Pentacles
cards.symbolism: A seated figure secures coins beneath both feet, against the chest and above the head.
cards.meaning: Protect the resources you need and be clear about what is enough.
cards.reversed: Notice when careful stewardship has become a grip that prevents useful exchange.

cards.title: Five of Pentacles
cards.symbolism: Two travelers pass through snow beneath a bright five-pentacle window.
cards.meaning: Acknowledge material difficulty and look for an accessible source of help.
cards.reversed: Accept a practical offer of support or make one easier to find.

cards.title: Six of Pentacles
cards.symbolism: A standing figure distributes coins while holding a balance.
cards.meaning: Consider both fairness and dignity in an exchange of support.
cards.reversed: Examine expectations that come attached to a gift or favor.

cards.title: Seven of Pentacles
cards.symbolism: A worker leans on a tool and studies the coins growing on a plant.
cards.meaning: Pause to assess the return on sustained effort before investing more.
cards.reversed: Adjust a plan whose demands have grown beyond its likely harvest.

cards.title: Eight of Pentacles
cards.symbolism: A seated worker carves one pentacle while finished pieces hang nearby.
cards.meaning: Repeat a focused practice and let each attempt improve the next.
cards.reversed: Change the exercise when repetition stops producing learning.

cards.title: Nine of Pentacles
cards.symbolism: A figure in a vineyard holds a hooded bird above nine pentacles.
cards.meaning: Enjoy the independence that patient care and practical skill have built.
cards.reversed: Review the price of maintaining a polished appearance of self-sufficiency.

cards.title: Ten of Pentacles
cards.symbolism: Ten coins frame figures of different generations beneath a stone arch.
cards.meaning: Think about the resources, practices and stories worth passing on.
cards.reversed: Discuss inherited expectations before allowing them to shape a shared future.

cards.title: Page of Pentacles
cards.symbolism: A youth studies a single pentacle closely in an open field.
cards.meaning: Turn interest into study by choosing a practical first exercise.
cards.reversed: Make the first assignment small enough to begin today.

cards.title: Knight of Pentacles
cards.symbolism: A knight sits on a motionless dark horse with a pentacle above plowed fields.
cards.meaning: Dependable, repeated effort can carry a long project forward.
cards.reversed: Refresh a routine that has become more rigid than useful.

cards.title: Queen of Pentacles
cards.symbolism: The queen cradles a pentacle in a flowering garden with a rabbit nearby.
cards.meaning: Express care through tangible support and the comforts of ordinary life.
cards.reversed: Include your own practical needs in the care you offer.

cards.title: King of Pentacles
cards.symbolism: A king holds a coin on a vine-covered throne above a prosperous landscape.
cards.meaning: Use established resources to create durable security for more than yourself.
cards.reversed: Check whether the wish to preserve comfort is crowding out generosity or change.
